body:
The historical sparse-fusion screen repeatedly computes identical binary ranks for triples related by spectator permutations. This adds an opt-in exact orbit reduction retaining every original check and receipt field. Status: verification tooling; no new kappa.

At h=25, unary rank calculations fall from 147,200 to 512. All 64 frame changes, 128 other frame ranks, 4,096 joint-pair ranks and 8,256 original predicate/message checks remain. A permutation-conjugation argument proves the reduction for the pinned identity-spectator geometry, including singular blocks.

Five alternating fresh-process A/B pairs on CPython 3.12.14 / macOS arm64 measured the complete historical certificate at 0.376574 s to 0.084435 s (4.460x). Central-screen ratios are 6.293x at h=25 and 8.440x at h=28. All 30 timed complete receipts match exactly. BENCHMARK.json retains raw samples, exact receipts, environment and source hashes. These are historical verifier measurements, not selected cold-replay or integer-multiplication timings; the host was not isolated.

Reproduce with Python 3.11+, standard library only, from the repository root:

    python3 -I -B research/sparse-fusion-orbits/verify.py
    python3 -I -O -B research/sparse-fusion-orbits/verify.py

Expected:

    PASS_SPARSE_FUSION_ORBITS frames=64 joint_pairs=4096 h=22,25,28 tests=12 kappa=unchanged

All 12 tests pass normally and under optimized Python. An independent row-elimination engine checks 455,424 frame/triple cases at h=22,25,28; explicit conjugations, full receipts and all original check traces agree. Negative controls detect changed weights, missing orbits, wrong representatives, source/certificate drift and two faulty rank kernels. A control demonstrates that final minima can hide a wrong representative; intermediate per-block totals detect it.

A minimal closure with spaces in its path passes the full optimized verifier without Git or unmanifested inputs. Typed-receipt corruption and output-preservation controls pass. Six unchanged historical tests pass with the original engine and with the accelerated engine under -O. Selected-record integrity, all 29 base Git blob/source bindings, exact published/local tree equality and whitespace/scope checks pass.

Only research/sparse-fusion-orbits/ is added. Original scripts, default commands, selected frontier and upstream/ remain unchanged. Exact base: f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631. Published head: 6e004d863bffd2d91b4168b78deb4e7b6fa1fe5e. SOURCES.json pins imported modules, receipts, context and upstream inputs with SHA-256 and Git blob identities. EXPECTED.json freezes full outputs; PROOF.md and VALIDATION.md record the argument, checks and limits.

The equivalence assumes the pinned identity spectator block, zero cross blocks, three distinguished coordinates and weight-three indicators. This does not reopen the closed central-frame search or discharge inherited all-size, realization, hosting, precision/tape or analytic obligations. Full make verify, selected cold reconstruction, Lean and hosted CI were not run or claimed.

OS assignment seed 91 selected verification engineering. No coordination issue exists; the local claim includes the result and source-branch link. Final overlap checks found no duplicate and main remained unchanged. Related PR871 applies modular rational-rank screening to another historical checker; PR824 changes stage-pair arithmetic. Neither is consumed.

Credit Douglas R. Colkitt for the original checker and finite obstruction, preserving manuscript and selected PR799/PR741/PR589/PR555 predecessor notices. Prepared for ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separately implemented AI checks and reviews. No independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0; see NOTICE.md.
title: Tooling: exact spectator orbits accelerate historical sparse-fusion verification
